script: My ex stole my 401k, I am about to expose a hidden revenge plan.. When our first baby hit the world, my ex made me quit my job, like, right after the birth. I didn't even have a job to go back to. Fast forward to when our second was two, I found out he was cheating. He'd already been verbally, emotionally, and sometimes physically abusive. When he got violent with our first kid, I kicked him out in 2012. I couldn't afford daycare, had no family help, and he said, "The courts haven't ordered me to give you a dime!" He even lied to the bank, got my accounts frozen, and hit me when I filed for default in the divorce. The judge finally forced him to pay child and spousal support six months after I sent him packing—$2,562 a month. He didn't start paying until the garnishment kicked in, so by then he was $6,000 behind. I used that to get permission to move away. I remarried a year after the divorce. I skimmed the court docs and saw a tiny box: "spousal support stops upon remarriage if checked." It wasn't checked, so I thought I was good. Instead of filing for his retirement, I just kept that first year of spousal support—$12k—and left it alone. (Spousal support was only ordered for two years.) In 2017, he filed for sole custody out of nowhere. That's when he learned I'd remarried and that I'd taken the $12k he'd paid me the first year. I told him I'd kept that money instead of fighting for his retirement. He demanded I repay the spousal support. The judge ordered me to repay it, but raised child support and deducted the repayment from that. I ended up with an extra $20 a month, and he basically paid himself back. He dropped his custody bid for two extra weeks of summer time. I went after the retirement account split. He was a nightmare, dragging it out for four years. They sanctioned him, and he had to pay me $600 a month for a year on top of child support. They even charged him with contempt. In January 2021, he proposed to his girlfriend. In May 2021, I finally got the disbursement from his 401(k). I won't say how much—it was about four times the overpayment of spousal support. I had no idea it'd be that much. I thought it'd be around $12k, which is why I thought keeping that year of spousal support instead of filing for his retirement was a fair trade. Had he not tried to take the kids from me, I never would've filed to split the account. Play stupid games… win stupid prizes. His fiancé emailed me recently and said it's my fault he won't marry her because I "cleaned out" his retirement account. She says I shouldn't have "stolen" his money. I told her I gave him the option to let me keep that year of spousal support or take it back and I could file for his retirement. He chose to have me file for his retirement. I said if he really wanted to marry her and protect his assets, they could get a prenup so he wouldn't have to worry. She said she shouldn't have to sign a prenup because I "robbed" him. I never asked to be financially dependent on him. He clearly wanted a court order to take care of his kids, so I got him one. I tried to be fair and take the lesser amount by keeping the spousal support and not filing for his retirement. He wouldn't let me. In short, my ex refused to pay me until support orders dropped, tried to get me in trouble for accepting spousal support over payment, and in the end it cost him a lot of money out of his 401(k).
